title: Three Questions of Erdős-Nathanson on Asymptotic Bases of Order 2
summary: We study three natural properties that measure the robustness of asymptotic bases of order 2: having divergent representation function, being decomposable as a union of two bases, and containing a minimal basis. Erdős and Nathanson showed that sufficiently rapid growth of the representation function (specifically, $r_A(n) \ge C \log n$ for appropriate $C$) implies both decomposability and the existence of a minimal basis. We prove that for weaker growth rates, these three properties are independent. The construction proceeds via an inductive scheme on exponentially growing intervals.
